scene.note: What Ailsa hears on the radio sits at the top of radio_log.py, and your code turns it into one tidy line for the callout log.

steps.note: The radio gives the hill and the grid reference as two pieces of text.
Under Task 1 they are joined into one location, with the words and spaces between them.
The location is kept in its own variable for the log entry later.
The call sign came off the radio form with stray spaces and in small letters.
Under Task 2 two methods tidy it: one removes the spaces at the ends, one makes capitals.
Every call sign in the log now looks the same.
How many went out arrives as a number, not as text.
Under Task 3 the number becomes text before it joins the words in front of it.
The crew line is text, ready to print or to join to more text.
The tidy call sign, the location and the crew are all ready.
Under Task 4 one f-string writes the whole entry, with each value in its place.
Ailsa's log gets the same kind of line for every callout.
